name: MutationObserver
description: Watches a DOM subtree for changes such as added/removed nodes, attribute changes, or text changes, and invokes a callback with a batch of mutations.
parameters: callback — function receiving (mutations, observer). observe() takes a target node and an options object (childList, attributes, subtree, etc.).
returns: A MutationObserver instance with observe()/disconnect() methods.
example:
const obs = new MutationObserver((muts) => console.log(muts));
obs.observe(el, { childList: true, subtree: true });
notes: Mutations are batched and delivered asynchronously via microtasks, not synchronously on every change.

name: IntersectionObserver
description: Asynchronously observes when a target element enters or exits the viewport (or another ancestor element), commonly used for lazy loading and infinite scroll.
parameters: callback — receives an array of IntersectionObserverEntry objects. options — root, rootMargin, threshold.
notes: Much more performant than listening to scroll events and computing getBoundingClientRect() manually.

name: ResizeObserver
description: Watches an element for changes to its content box or border box size and invokes a callback whenever it resizes.
parameters: callback — receives an array of ResizeObserverEntry objects.
notes: Useful for responsive components that need to react to their own container size rather than the viewport.

name: requestAnimationFrame()
description: Schedules a callback to run before the browser's next repaint, ideal for smooth, jank-free visual updates.
returns: A request id usable with cancelAnimationFrame().
notes: Automatically throttles/pauses in background tabs, unlike setTimeout/setInterval, making it the right tool for animations.

name: FormData
description: Builds a set of key/value pairs from a form's fields, suitable for submitting via fetch() including file inputs.
parameters: formElement — optional HTMLFormElement to pre-populate from.
returns: A FormData instance with get()/set()/append()/entries() methods.
example:
const data = new FormData(document.querySelector('form'));
fetch('/submit', { method: 'POST', body: data });
notes: Automatically sets the correct multipart/form-data Content-Type when used as a fetch body, including file uploads.

name: matchMedia()
description: Evaluates a CSS media query in JavaScript and returns an object that can be checked immediately and listened to for changes.
parameters: mediaQueryString — a CSS media query, e.g. '(max-width: 600px)'.
returns: A MediaQueryList with a matches boolean and addEventListener('change', ...).
example:
const mq = window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)');
mq.addEventListener('change', (e) => console.log(e.matches));
notes: The recommended way to react to responsive breakpoints or system preferences (dark mode, reduced motion) in JS.

name: getBoundingClientRect()
description: Returns the size and position of an element relative to the viewport.
returns: A DOMRect with top, right, bottom, left, width and height properties.
notes: Values are relative to the current viewport, so they change as the page scrolls — call it fresh whenever needed rather than caching it.

name: localStorage
description: A key-value web storage API that persists string data in the browser with no expiration, scoped per origin.
parameters: key/value — both strings; objects must be serialized with JSON.stringify()/JSON.parse().
returns: getItem() returns the string value or null if not set.
notes: Storage operations are synchronous and can block the main thread with large data; not accessible from Web Workers or across origins.

name: sessionStorage
description: A key-value web storage API identical to localStorage in interface, but scoped to a single browser tab/session and cleared when that tab closes.
returns: getItem() returns the string value or null if not set.
notes: Unlike localStorage, data is not shared between tabs even on the same origin.

name: ResizeObserver vs window resize event
description: The window 'resize' event only fires when the entire browser viewport changes, while ResizeObserver detects size changes of any individual element regardless of cause (e.g. content change, flex layout shifts).
notes: Prefer ResizeObserver when you need to react to a specific element's size rather than the whole window.
